replies.user: [BASICS: Unit 1, Lesson 1] Teach me what an AI chatbot is, in plain words. Keep it short, then let me try one.
replies.raw:
Welcome. You can't break anything here, and there are no silly questions.

If something goes wrong, we start again.

Type in the box at the bottom, or tap the microphone on your keyboard and talk. Then tap the arrow to send.

An **AI chatbot** is a computer program you talk to by typing or speaking. It writes back in everyday words.

No one is typing back to you.

Try asking me: "Are you a real person?"

No. I'm Merc, a chatbot in a learning app. No one is typing back to you.

Practicing on me works the same way as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Copilot.

Notice that you asked a plain question, and you got a plain answer. That's all it takes.

Now ask me anything you're curious about.

replies.user: How do I keep basil alive on a windowsill?
replies.raw:
Basil likes a lot of light and steady water. Here is what helps most.

1. Put it in a window that gets 6 hours of sun. A south-facing one is best.
2. Water when the top of the soil feels dry. Let extra water drain out.
3. Pinch off the top leaves often. That makes the plant grow bushy.
4. Keep it away from cold glass in winter. Basil hates the cold.

If the leaves turn yellow, it usually needs less water. If it gets tall and thin, it needs more light.

Notice that I gave you steps you can use today. You asked about a real plant, and that's how to get useful help.

A chatbot like me learned from a huge amount of writing. It makes each answer by guessing, word by word, what fits best.

It isn't a person, and it isn't a search engine. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Copilot work this way too.

Tap the answer you think is right. There's no grade.

[KEY]A chatbot is a program that writes answers by guessing what words fit best.[/KEY]

[Q]
Which is the best description of an AI chatbot?
A) A person at the company reading your messages and typing answers back to you
B) A computer program that writes answers by guessing what words fit best
C) A big library of checked facts that looks up the one right answer every time
ANS: B
[/Q]

replies.user: I picked B) A computer program that writes answers by guessing what words fit best
replies.raw:
That's right. It guesses what fits best, and it's not a person or a library of checked facts.

You asked about your own basil, and that's how to get good help.

Here's one rule to keep: if you wouldn't write it on a postcard, don't type it into a chatbot.

replies.user: [BASICS: Unit 2, Lesson 4] Teach me about AI voice-clone and family emergency scams, and exactly what to do if I get one of those calls. Then help me make a plan.
replies.raw:
Last time, you learned the postcard rule.

Here is something worth knowing. AI can copy a person's voice from a short recording, like a video posted online.

Scammers use this to sound like a grandchild or other relative in trouble.

Even if the caller's name or number shows on your screen, callers can fake that too. So don't trust the voice.

[KEY]A voice can be faked, so hang up and call back on a number you already know.[/KEY]

Here are the warning signs:

- It's urgent.
- It's a secret ("don't tell Mom").
- They want cash, gift cards, or money sent from your bank.

[EX]In 2023, an Arizona mother got a call. Her 15-year-old daughter was safe the whole time. But a voice that sounded exactly like her daughter asked for help, and a man demanded money. The mother later told the U.S. Senate about it.[/EX]

A code word is a word only your family knows. If a caller can't say it, hang up.

Try asking me: "Write a text asking my family to pick a code word."

replies.user: Write a text asking my family to pick a code word.
replies.raw:
Here is a text you can send:

"Hi all. Scammers can now copy a person's voice with AI. So I'd like us to pick a family code word. It should be a word only we know, and not something people could find online.

If anyone ever calls asking for money or help, we ask for the code word first. If they can't say it, we hang up and call back.

Can we pick one this week? Please tell me yours when we talk in person or on a call you know is real."

Don't tell me the actual code word. Keep that for your family.

Notice how the text says what to do if the caller can't give the word. That gives your family a clear next step.

Now try: "Make it short and friendly."

Here is a shorter, friendlier version:

"Hi family! Let's pick a secret code word that only we know. If anyone calls asking for money or help, we ask for it first. No word, no help.

Let's choose one this week."

Notice what changed. It's about a third as long, but it still says what the word is for.

Here is the second part of the plan. If a call like this comes, hang up and call the person back.

Use your contacts or a number you already know. If you can't reach them, call someone else in the family, even if you were told to keep it secret.

Hanging up won't hurt them. If it's real, they will still be okay in the five minutes it takes to check.

[KEY]If a call asks for money in a hurry, hang up and call back on a number you know.[/KEY]

[Q]
A call sounds exactly like your grandson. He's crying, says he's in jail, and asks you to buy gift cards and keep it secret. What do you do first?
A) Buy the gift cards right away, so he's safe and doesn't get in more trouble
B) Hang up and call him, or his parents, on a number you already know
C) Ask the caller for a phone number where you can call him back right away
ANS: B
[/Q]

replies.user: I picked C) Ask the caller for a phone number where you can call him back right away
replies.raw:
C is a very natural pick, and it's the one that catches many people. A number the caller gives you goes straight back to the scammer.

They can answer it and keep playing the part.

Here is a different example. Say a caller claims to be your niece and gives you a "new number" to reach her.

If you call it, the scammer picks up. The only safe number is one you already had, like the one in your contacts.

If you can't reach her there, call someone else in the family. Even if you were told to keep it secret.

[Q]
A call sounds exactly like your grandson. He's crying, says he's in jail, and asks you to buy gift cards and keep it secret. What do you do first?
A) Buy the gift cards right away, so he's safe and doesn't get in more trouble
B) Hang up and call him, or his parents, on a number you already know
C) Ask the caller for a phone number where you can call him back right away
ANS: B
[/Q]

replies.user: I picked B) Hang up and call him, or his parents, on a number you already know
replies.raw:
That's right. A number you already know leads to the real person, not to the caller.

You wrote a code-word text and then made it shorter, and that gave your family a plan they can use. Your own plan now has two parts: a code word, and a hang-up and call-back.

Try this today: Send the code-word text to your family.
